steps.title: Shoulder joint
steps.body: Ball-and-socket joint allowing a wide range of movement including flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation and circumduction.

steps.title: Elbow joint
steps.body: Hinge joint allowing only flexion and extension.

steps.title: Hip joint
steps.body: Ball-and-socket joint allowing flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, rotation and circumduction.

steps.title: Knee joint
steps.body: Hinge joint (modified) allowing primarily flexion and extension, with slight rotation when flexed.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Identify the joint, movement and agonist muscle when a cricketer bowls the ball forward. | Describe the movement at the knee during the upward phase of a squat and name the agonist muscle. | What movement occurs at the shoulder during the arm-raising phase of a star jump? Name the agonist muscle.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Joint: Shoulder (ball-and-socket). Movement: Flexion (the arm swings forwards and upwards). Agonist: Anterior deltoids and pectorals. | Movement: Extension at the knee (the angle increases as the leg straightens). Agonist: Quadriceps contract concentrically. | Movement: Abduction at the shoulder (the arms move away from the midline of the body). Agonist: Deltoids (middle fibres).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give: joint → movement → muscle, in that order Use the correct joint name (shoulder, elbow, hip, knee, ankle) - don't say "arm" or "leg" Use precise movement terms: flexion/extension, abduction/adduction, plantar flexion/dorsiflexion Name the specific muscle as the agonist - don't just say "the muscle" Practise analysing a range of sporting actions - this is a very common 4-6 mark question Remember: hinge joints (elbow, knee, ankle) only allow flexion/extension; ball-and-socket (shoulder, hip) allow all movements
